_finding: The owner asked for his own address and the server's own traffic to be left out of the statistics. A request we ignore must leave no row at all, and only the address it really is: a neighbouring address, or one that merely begins with the same digits, must still be counted, and a mistyped entry must never widen the list.

mutations.name: a page load is counted whoever asks
mutations.find: load (ip, headers, page) { if (off || ignored(ip, headers['user-agent'])) return;
mutations.expect: FAIL a configured address is not counted

mutations.name: a beacon is counted whoever sends it
mutations.find: hit (ip, headers, hit) { if (off || ignored(ip, headers['user-agent'])) return;
mutations.expect: FAIL an ignored beacon, action and MCP call write nothing either

mutations.name: a range matches on whole bytes only, so a /26 covers the whole /24
mutations.expect: FAIL a range matches by bits, not by text

mutations.name: an entry of one family is matched against an address of the other
mutations.find: entries.some((e) => e.bytes.length === bytes.length && samePrefix(e.bytes, bytes, e.bits))
mutations.expect: FAIL an IPv4 entry never matches an IPv6 address, or the other way round

mutations.name: a host that cannot read its own addresses says nothing, as on 13.11
mutations.expect: FAIL a host whose own addresses cannot be read says so, and still ignores loopback

mutations.name: a malformed entry becomes a range that covers everything
mutations.find:
const bytes = ipBytes(addr)
  if (!bytes) return null
mutations.expect: FAIL comments, blank lines, commas and spaces are read; bad words are counted, not kept
